title: Mara and the Garden
premise: Wren Blackwood has spent his life in the valley of Vell, where magic cannot cross the border stones and his runaway apprenticeship to a hedge-witch bought him safety from the sorcerous Order that trained him. When a date he's arranged with a stranger named Mara appears verbatim in a century-old book of prophecies, he learns the prophecy foretells a 'doorkeeper' who will reopen the way into Aldermere—a country erased by the long winter and ruled by the Order's corrupted founder. Mara is not a stranger but an exile from Aldermere, sent to find him because only someone born on both sides of the border can walk through doors that no longer exist. Pursued by the Order's frost-bound hunters, Wren must choose between the invisible life he built and the duty he never asked for, discovering along the way that his own magic was never lost—only buried. In the end, Wren opens the door not by power but by surrendering his claim to it, letting Mara carry the crown she fled, while he remains the keeper of the threshold: loved, seen, and finally at home in himself.
about_author: Beatrix Fairweather is the pen name of a former botanist who traded field notebooks for fantasy manuscripts after a decade cataloguing alpine flora. She writes stories about borders, gardens, and the people who grow in the cracks between them.

chapters.title: The Valley Where Magic Cannot Follow
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. We meet Wren tending bees and hiding his scarred hands, the mark of the apprenticeship he fled years ago. He prepares for a first date with a woman he met through letters, terrified and hopeful. Emotional beat: longing for connection warring with the instinct to stay small and unseen.

chapters.title: A Date Written in Ink
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Mara arrives—and so does a traveling peddler selling old books, one of which contains a prophecy describing tonight word for word, down to the spilled cider. Wren realizes his life has been scripted for a century. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread as invisibility proves impossible.

chapters.title: What Mara Carried Across the Snow
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. She confesses she is from Aldermere, the country swallowed by the long winter, and that she was sent to find the doorkeeper named in the prophecy—Wren. She shows him a living seed from Aldermere's royal garden, still warm. Emotional beat: guilt over using him, tangled with genuine falling-in-love.

chapters.title: Hunters in White
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The Order's frost-bound hunters reach the valley's edge; the border stones are failing. Wren's buried magic stirs for the first time when he shields Mara, burning his scars anew. Emotional beat: terror of his own power, and the corrupting sweetness of feeling strong again.

chapters.title: The Hedge-Witch's Last Lesson
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. They seek Wren's old teacher, who reveals why magic fails in the valley: it isn't dead here—it's imprisoned, and Wren's bloodline helped build the prison. She gives him a key made of thorn and glass before the hunters take her. Emotional beat: grief, and the weight of inherited complicity.

chapters.title: Doors That No Longer Exist
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Following the key, the pair finds the door hidden inside a hollowed oak—but opening it requires Wren to embrace the full magic he fled, which whispers promises of power. He refuses, and the door stays shut. Emotional beat: the first real test of love against ambition; Mara sees him fail and loves him anyway.

chapters.title: The Founder's Bargain
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Captured briefly by the hunters' captain, Mara learns the Order's founder is the winter itself, sustained by the stolen magic of the valley, and that he wants Wren as a vessel. She bargains her royal blood for Wren's freedom. Emotional beat: duty consuming love, as she becomes what she fled—a piece on the board.

chapters.title: Where the Long Winter Falls
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren walks into the winter alone to trade himself for Mara, confronting the founder, who offers him everything he secretly wanted: mastery, recognition, an end to hiding. Wren nearly accepts. Emotional beat: the darkest hour—the corruption of power dressed as belonging.

chapters.title: The Doorkeeper's Choice
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the climax, Wren understands the door was never locked—it waits for someone to stop grasping. He surrenders his claim to power entirely, and the prison breaks open, flooding the valley's magic back into the world and shattering the founder's winter. Mara takes up her crown. Emotional beat: liberation through renunciation.

chapters.title: Mara and the Garden
chapters.summary: Both POVs, closing together. Spring crosses the restored border; Aldermere's garden blooms again under Queen Mara. Wren, offered a place at her side, chooses instead to keep the threshold between worlds—visited, loved, no longer invisible. Final image: two chairs in a garden, one facing each country. Emotional beat: peace, identity chosen rather than imposed.
